questions.answer: The centre of gravity is the point through which the whole weight of a body may be considered to act. The moment of a force about a point is the product of the force and the perpendicular distance from the point to the line of action of the force.
accepted_alternatives: For centre of gravity: the point at which all the weight of a body appears to act.
questions.unit_policy: No unit is required for definitions.
questions.tolerance: Accept equivalent controlled wording only when both the whole weight and perpendicular line-of-action distance meanings remain unambiguous.

option_feedback.A: The geometric centre is valid only for suitable symmetric uniform objects, not every non-uniform object.
option_feedback.B: Correct. The distributed gravitational effect is represented by the whole weight acting vertically downward through the centre of gravity.
option_feedback.C: A support point is not automatically the centre of gravity.
option_feedback.D: Weight acts vertically downward, not horizontally.

questions.answer: Represent the distributed weight by one vertical downward force through the centre of gravity. W = mg = 3.6 x 9.81 = 35.316 N. M = Wd_perp = 35.316 x 0.42 = 14.83272 N m, so the moment is 15 N m clockwise to two significant figures.
questions.unit_policy: Force must be in N and moment in N m; equivalent converted moment units are accepted with correct working.
questions.tolerance: Accept 14.8 N m to 15.0 N m for correctly rounded work using g = 9.81 N kg^-1.

questions.answer: W = mg = 8.0 x 9.81 = 78.48 N. The perpendicular distance to the vertical line of action is the horizontal separation d_perp = 0.75 cos 40 degrees = 0.5745 m. M = 78.48 x 0.5745 = 45.1 N m, so the moment is 45 N m clockwise to two significant figures. When the panel is vertical with its centre of gravity directly above the hinge, the weight's line of action passes through the hinge, so d_perp = 0 and the moment is 0 N m.
accepted_alternatives: 45.1 N m clockwise and 0 N m when vertical
45 N m clockwise and 0 N m when vertical
